title: Nothing Before Seventy
thesis: Hokusai graded his own life's work by age, and the most reproduced print in the world falls inside the years he wrote off.

record: An ōban nishiki-e sheet, Edo c. 1800–1849: washi substrate, key block plus flat opaque colour blocks, kentō registration, publisher and censor seals, a vertical signature column inside the image field.

narration.why: an imported voice, marked as ours rather than passed off as his

motion.models: the baren's stroke: it bites at once, rubs out along the block, stops

name: The verdict
claim: there is nothing worth taking into account
pre: of all I drew by my seventieth year
lede: He was seventy-three when he wrote that, and he had fifteen years left. The sentence keeps going, and it keeps counting: eighty-six, ninety, a hundred, a hundred and ten. Eight attainments, eight ages. Three of them fall after the end of his life.
note: Colophon to One Hundred Views of Mount Fuji, 1834
foot: Scroll — his scale builds first, and empty

name: The tail
claim: He forecast three more attainments and reached none of them.
lede: He forecast three more attainments — at ninety, at a hundred, at a hundred and ten. He died at eighty-eight, and no work stands in any of them.

reveal.claim: He was between sixty-eight and seventy-two.
reveal.narr: c. 1829–1832 — the bar crosses his line at seventy. The most reproduced image in the world was made inside the years its author wrote off.
reveal.low: You put it at age {g}, which is inside them too.

why: A woodblock has no continuous tone: at every point the ink is either laid or it is not. That is a dither, moving at the speed of a swell.
The plate turns to sumi at eighty-eight; the grain drifts slowly enough to read as night rather than as an empty div.

rationale: His voice, and nothing else. Sampled from the deep blue field of Fine Wind, Clear Morning. Every register label on the plot is his own wording.

Posterity, and the arithmetic this page did that the article did not. Sampled from the vermilion ground of the Dragon on the Higashimachi Festival Float, Obuse, 1844. It is a seal, never a tint of text.
The paper margin of the surimono Still Life, with its fibre kept rather than cleaned off. The rules are key-block lines, because a print outlines every region before it colours one.
Newsreader for narration — an imported voice, and marked as ours. A Japanese gothic for dates, sources and measurements: the register the museums that hold him set their labels in.

Every age on the plot. The article gives years; the ages are years less a birth of c. 1760, which the infobox itself calls supposed. Wherever a number was calculated rather than read, the seal is stamped beside it.
